column1: Break up the cold day-old rice with your fingers so there are no clumps. Don't use freshly cooked rice; it's too wet and turns mushy.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper. Cook in a lightly oiled 8-inch pan over medium-high heat until about half set, flip briefly, then cut into small squares without letting it dry out.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat a wok or large pan over high heat with a little oil and sear the chicken in batches until golden on all sides. Set aside.
Add about 1 tsp oil, the white parts of the spring onions, and the bell pepper to the hot pan and cook until browned.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds.
Add the rice, chicken, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil and mix well over high heat.
Press the rice flat and leave it 2–3 minutes to form a crust, then stir. Repeat about 6 times.
Stir in the green onion tops and the omelette pieces and serve right away.
